note: Empty because the fixture runs against an empty home, and with no ~/.minimax/config.yaml there is no provider for this adapter to redirect -- which is the launch it is supposed to produce then. Given a config it sets MINIMAX_DATA_DIR to <runDir>/mcode-data and writes the redirected config there; that path is checked in test/mcode.test.ts, where the file can actually be read. MCode keeps its origin in that config and uses Node's fetch, which consults neither HTTP_PROXY nor HTTPS_PROXY, so the base-URL route has no variable to set and --tls-intercept sees nothing at all -- a run recorded that way ends with capture.empty. Verified against @minimax-ai/code 0.4.12 by running it: `orca record mcode -- exec --prompt-mode coding --permission off --max-steps 1 'Reply with exactly: ADAPTER-OK'` recorded 14 events and 6 exchanges, and the request carries a 16,162-character system prompt beginning 'You run inside MiniMax Code, a workspace developed by MiniMax'. The gateway answered 401 -- which is the point: the key in the generated config is the placeholder, because the file lands inside the run directory and a credential is never written there, and the prompt is captured anyway since it travels in the request. Each provider's origin is carried through /forward/ so the call still names the host the operator configured; the run logged upstream=http://155.103.159.98:8317, theirs. Only custom providers can be captured: on that same run MCode rewrote exactly two lines of the generated config on startup, the built-in minimax_api provider's baseURL and apiKey, restoring its own values -- which is also why the data directory is moved rather than the operator's file edited in place.
